reference.title: Scenario 7: Two-level nested numbered list (sub steps) in a procedure
reference.shortdesc: Consider a procedure for creating an alarm notification that contains major steps and subordinate actions.

section.p: Consider a procedure for creating an alarm notification that contains major steps and subordinate actions.

entry.codeblock: # Creating an Alarm Notification 1. Create the notification. 1. Click **Add Notification**. 2. Enter the notification name. 3. Select the notification type. 2. Configure notification recipients. 1. Add recipient email addresses. 2. Configure escalation contacts. 3. Save the notification.

<task id="creating_an_alarm_notification"> <title>Creating an Alarm Notification</title> <taskbody> <steps> <step> <cmd>Create the notification.</cmd> <substeps> <substep> <cmd>Click <uicontrol>Add Notification</uicontrol>.</cmd> </substep> <substep> <cmd>Enter the notification name.</cmd> </substep> <substep> <cmd>Select the notification type.</cmd> </substep> </substeps> </step> <step> <cmd>Configure notification recipients.</cmd> <substeps> <substep> <cmd>Add recipient email addresses.</cmd> </substep> <substep> <cmd>Configure escalation contacts.</cmd> </substep> </substeps> </step> <step> <cmd>Save the notification.</cmd> </step> </steps> </taskbody> </task>

section.p: Result: The converter recognizes the nested ordered list structure and generates DITA <substeps> elements beneath the corresponding parent steps. The hierarchy of the source Markdown list is preserved in the generated DITA task topic.
